title: Sicilian Defence
intro: 1.e4 c5: Black fights for the centre from the side and plays for a win. The most popular answer to 1.e4.

lessons.title: The Open Sicilian and the Najdorf
lessons.summary: Trade a side pawn for a centre pawn, then a6.

steps.text: White opens with 1.e4. The Sicilian answers 1...c5: the pawn controls d4 from the side and keeps the game unbalanced.
White develops with 2.Nf3, getting ready for d4.
Play d6: it guards e5 and prepares ...Nf6.
steps.hint: A one-square pawn move in the centre.
steps.ifWrong: This lesson follows the main line with 2...d6.

feedback.b8c6: 2...Nc6 is a popular Sicilian move too. This lesson follows 2...d6.
feedback.e7e6: 2...e6 is a popular Sicilian move too. This lesson follows 2...d6.

steps.text: Take on d4. You swap your side pawn for White's centre pawn.
steps.ifRight: Now you have two centre pawns against White's one.

steps.text: White takes back with the knight: 4.Nxd4.
Develop with an attack on e4.
steps.hint: Your king's knight can hit e4.
steps.ifWrong: Bring out the knight so it attacks e4.

steps.text: White defends with 5.Nc3. Now you choose your Sicilian.
Play the Najdorf: the quiet a6 keeps White's pieces off b5 and prepares ...e5 or ...b5.
steps.hint: A one-square move with the a-pawn.
steps.ifRight: The Najdorf, a favourite of world champions.

feedback.g7g6: That is the Dragon: also excellent, with the bishop going to g7. This lesson shows the Najdorf.

steps.text: Your plan: use the half-open c-file (a rook on c8 later), challenge the centre with ...e5 or ...e6, and expand with ...b5.
